items.followUp: Write two properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: One valid physical property of covalent compounds is required.
rubric.description: States one characteristic property of covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct property, such as low melting/boiling points, poor electrical conductivity, or solubility in organic solvents.

rubric.why: A second distinct property completes the response.
rubric.description: States a second characteristic property of covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different correct property.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They do not conduct electricity in the solid or liquid state.

rubric.why: The definition identifies absolute zero as the lowest possible temperature.
rubric.description: Defines absolute zero as the lowest possible temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the lowest possible temperature or the temperature at which particles have minimum kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The temperature value is an essential part of the answer.
rubric.description: Gives the value of absolute zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 0 K or approximately −273 °C (−273.15 °C).

modelAnswer: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, at which particles have minimum kinetic energy.
Its value is 0 K, or approximately −273 °C.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the change from liquid to solid.
rubric.description: Identifies the change of state involved in freezing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a liquid changes into a solid.

rubric.why: Freezing point is the temperature at which the phase change occurs under a specified pressure.
rubric.description: States that freezing occurs at a definite temperature under a given pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the change occurs at a fixed temperature at a given pressure.

modelAnswer: The freezing point is the temperature at which a liquid changes into a solid.
It is measured at a specified pressure.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a saturated solution and an unsaturated solution?

rubric.why: A dilute solution contains relatively little dissolved solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a dilute solution has a relatively small amount of solute compared with the amount of solvent or solution.

rubric.why: A concentrated solution contains relatively more dissolved solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a concentrated solution has a relatively large amount of solute compared with the amount of solvent or solution.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a relatively small amount of solute compared with the amount of solvent.
A concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute compared with the amount of solvent.

rubric.why: The numerator must be the volume of the solute.
rubric.description: Identifies the volume used in the v/m percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the volume of solute, usually in millilitres.

rubric.why: The denominator and percentage basis specify the mass of solution per 100 parts.
rubric.description: States the mass basis and the percentage definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining v/m % as the volume of solute per 100 units of mass of solution, or giving the equivalent formula.

modelAnswer: Percentage volume/mass (v/m %) is the volume of solute, in millilitres, present in 100 grams of solution.
v/m % = (volume of solute in mL ÷ mass of solution in g) × 100

items.followUp: What is the Tyndall effect, and which type of mixture shows it?

rubric.why: True-solution particles are too small to scatter visible light.
rubric.description: Explains the small size of particles in a true solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solute particles are extremely small (molecular or ionic in size).

rubric.why: The absence of light scattering explains why the effect is not seen.
rubric.description: Connects small particle size to the absence of the Tyndall effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles do not scatter light, so the Tyndall effect is not observed.

modelAnswer: The particles in a true solution are extremely small, generally molecular or ionic in size.
They do not scatter light; therefore, true solutions do not show the Tyndall effect.

items.followUp: Write any two uses of potassium.

rubric.why: Sodium is used in sodium-vapour lamps, including street lighting.
rubric.description: Gives one valid use of sodium in lamps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sodium-vapour or street lamps as a use.

rubric.why: Sodium is also used as a heat-transfer medium in some nuclear reactors.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid use of sodium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its use as a coolant or heat-transfer medium in nuclear reactors.

modelAnswer: Sodium is used in sodium-vapour lamps, including street lamps.
Liquid sodium is used as a coolant or heat-transfer medium in some nuclear reactors.

items.followUp: Why is pure gold usually mixed with other metals before making jewellery?

rubric.description: States that pure silver is soft.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the softness of pure silver.

rubric.why: Silver is alloyed to improve its hardness and durability.
rubric.description: Explains why silver is alloyed rather than used pure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is mixed with a metal such as copper to make it harder or more durable.

modelAnswer: Pure silver is soft and can be easily scratched or deformed.
It is therefore alloyed, commonly with copper, to make it harder and more durable.
